To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a wide-field space telescope with 1 m aperture, 2 arcsec seeing, 2% flat fielding accuracy, and 0.1% photometric accuracy can measure the lens power spectrum with 1% precision in 1 year of observations.

a wide-field space mission will be capable of measuring the matter density and dark energy equation-of- state parameters with an accuracy comparable to that from supernova surveys, and that this accuracy will be achieved if a large fraction (at least 20%) of the total survey area is covered with a small number of deep fields.

the lensing power-spectrum and skewness measurements are complementary and that a space mission with the SNAP-like specifications will be able to constrain the matter density and the dark energy parameters with a precision that is comparable and nearly orthogonal with the supernova measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a future wide-field imaging space telescope that is optimized for the study of weak gravitational lensing.
a future wide-field weak lensing survey from space.
how the lensing signal from space can be used to set constraints on cosmology and what the optimal survey design is.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a space-based wide-field survey with a 2 m telescope, a 2° field of view, and a seeing of 0.5 arcsec will be able to constrain the cosmological parameters with a precision comparable to that of supernovae and complementary to that of cosmic microwave background measurements.
weak lensing from space can provide competitive constraints on cosmological parameter, especially when combined with supernovae.
weak lensing will be a powerful cosmological probe from space and that a space telescope such as SNAP is a good investment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a wide-field survey with 0.1% photometric accuracy and a 10% sky coverage will provide a powerful cosmological tool.
a wide-field space telescope is the most promising instrument to study the large-scale structure of the universe and measure the cosmological parameters.

a future wide-field, space-based telescope will be able to constrain cosmological parameters from weak lensing with an accuracy that is comparable to the accuracy that can be achieved with the SNAP mission from supernovae, with a synergy that will be useful for cross-checking systematic errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a future space mission with a wide-field camera and a high-resolution imager can make significant improvements on the constraints on cosmological parameter from the weak lensing power spectrum.
weak lensing from space can provide a unique probe of dark matter and dark energy.
a wide-field space telescope is an ideal platform to measure the lensing signal and thus set constraints that are nearly orthogonal to those obtained from other probes such as supernovae.
